question: Does the already fitted, family-excluded E195 state baseline reduce the full-parameter trace variance of the unclipped four-episode score-function estimator relative to the original leave-other-three-out estimator?
limits: Not clipped PPO, minibatch averaging, random menu-count normalization, AdamW, or causal policy improvement.

The original state baseline fits exclude each held family. Folds share fitting data, so their outputs are dependent; fold-conditional bootstraps are descriptive. The all-family aggregate interval is descriptive only and has no confirmatory population interpretation.
Historical data and earlier prediction results were already examined. This retrospective audit does not remove cross-experiment selection or quantify uncertainty from refitting nuisance predictors.
Conditional independence concerns four independent policy sampling streams under the same game family and fixed initial actor; hidden game RNG is unchanged.
An unbiased four-observation variance estimate can be negative. These values are retained without clipping or outcome-based exclusions.
This result cannot reopen binary whole-game/four-rollout/shared-advantage recipe or justify extra training using a proxy.
No change to policy adoption, current simulator scope, full-game scores, or unused 512/1024 acceptance.
scope: Retrospective diagnostic of the existing E195 predictor; no new policy experiment.

root_receipt.independent_formula: squared norm of observed LOO mean minus average disjoint-pair kernel product; state score covariance from an 8x8 Gram transform

coverage: exact finite-distribution gradient means and variance estimates
better return prediction can increase score-function variance
negative variance estimates and all-failure groups retained

decision: Fixed diagnostic completes without its predeclared robust-variance support. Positive point estimates preserve the baseline hypothesis, but do not establish variance reduction or policy benefit. No predictor refit, gradient-variance grid, actor update, data expansion, or natural evaluation is admitted.

literature.use: Baseline prediction accuracy and gradient-estimator variance are distinct. The cited paper studies average reward/GPOMDP; this finite-episodic audit uses its own four-rollout estimator and exact-enumeration tests, not an unqualified transfer of that theorem.
